segments.title: 第31章 彩禮?
segments.content:
`Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 31: Bride Price?`

Li Luo was busy in the kitchen, prepping the ingredients alone.

Just as he was about to start cooking, he realized they were out of salt. He quickly called for Zhao Rongjun to go downstairs and buy some.

Zhao Rongjun, who had long fallen silent in the female-dominated territory, heard Li Luo's voice and felt as if he had received an imperial decree of amnesty. He bolted downstairs without a moment's hesitation.

After returning with the salt, Zhao Rongjun used the opportunity to stay in the kitchen and help Li Luo out.

"This personality of yours, not being able to talk much with girls, when are you going to change it?"

"I can talk, I just don't want to," Zhao Rongjun said stubbornly.

"Then let me ask you a question." Li Luo spoke as he cooked. "You have to answer me honestly."

"Go ahead."

"Suppose," Li Luo began, "you have a girlfriend, and it's time to discuss marriage. Her family demands a bride price of 300,000 yuan before you can marry. Would you pay it?"

"300,000?!" Zhao Rongjun's expression was one of shock, and he blurted out, "Is she robbing me?"

"So your answer is?"

"I'd have to be crazy to give her 300,000." Zhao Rongjun shook his head repeatedly. "Why doesn't she just go rob a bank?"

"Good!" Li Luo patted his shoulder. "Remember what you said today. Eat a bit more later."

"What do you mean by that?" Zhao Rongjun couldn't help but look suspicious. "Asking such a strange question out of the blue."

"Yeah," Li Luo rolled his eyes. "It is pretty strange. It's good that you know. Pass me the soy sauce."

"Oh, okay."

"Light soy sauce, not dark soy sauce. You grabbed the wrong one."

"Is there a difference?"

"One is for flavoring, the other is for color. You should learn a thing or two."

...

At six-thirty in the evening, a table full of dishes was brought to the dining table in the living room, steaming and fragrant.

Zhao Rongjun's eyes widened in disbelief. He never thought Li Luo could actually whip up such a feast.

Beside him, Xu Youyu was also quite surprised, glancing from time to time at the composed Li Luo, thinking to herself that this guy was not only a brilliant writer but also an excellent cook.

Aside from instant noodles, she had never cooked a meal for herself.

Ying Chanxi, however, was already used to it.

After all, ever since tasting Li Luo's fried noodles and learning that he had cooked the meal on the day her dad returned, Ying Chanxi had gained a clear understanding of Li Luo's culinary skills.

At this moment, Ying Chanxi calmly brought out bowls and chopsticks from the kitchen, handed them to Xu Youyu and Zhao Rongjun, then sat down next to Li Luo and said, "Let's eat, everyone."

The four of them sat around the table to eat. It had to be said, the feeling was rather novel.

They were all just fifteen or sixteen-year-old kids, and three of them were new first-years in high school this year.

Even the oldest, Xu Youyu, was only a second-year high school girl, not yet fully mature.

When she was renting the place alone, the feeling wasn't as profound.

Now, gathered around the dining table, eating with peers and with no adults around, it felt truly novel, and a little wonderful.

It was like secretly wearing a father's suit or a mother's high heels, a fresh feeling of imitating adult maturity.

It was very much like the fun of playing house as a child, only this was like a teenage version of playing house.

"So delicious." Xu Youyu took a bite of the Mapo Tofu, her eyes instantly lighting up.

It was her favorite dish, and the one Li Luo had made tasted remarkably similar to her mother's. It was absolutely delicious.

Hearing Xu Youyu's praise, Li Luo smiled silently.

Of tonight's six dishes and one soup, the Cola Chicken Wings and Scrambled Eggs with Tomato were Ying Chanxi's favorites.

The two dishes closest to Xu Youyu, Mapo Tofu and Stir-fried Pork with Green Peppers, were, in Li Luo's memory, probably her favorites.

As for the remaining two, Braised Beef Brisket with Potatoes and Stir-fried Vermicelli with Bean Sprouts, were both dishes that Zhao Rongjun enjoyed.

He had, in a way, catered to everyone's tastes.

Zhao Rongjun initially looked a bit skeptical, wondering if Xu Youyu's reaction was an exaggeration and if the food could really be that good.

But after taking a bite of Li Luo's cooking, he was completely stunned.

"It tastes a lot like what you'd get at a restaurant," Zhao Rongjun couldn't help but say. "Where did you learn to cook like this?"

Heh.

Li Luo chuckled to himself, thinking, *Do you think the chef's certificate I spent two and a half years studying for at the vocational college was for nothing?*

But what he said was a complete fabrication: "I'm self-taught, a natural talent."

"I'd have to be a ghost to believe you," Zhao Rongjun said, looking exasperated.

But on second thought, Zhao Rongjun remembered Li Luo's high school entrance exam scores and considered the effort this guy might have put in behind the scenes. He figured that for Li Luo, learning to cook probably wasn't such a difficult thing after all.

"Senior Sister, have you never cooked here before?" Ying Chanxi asked curiously as they ate.

"How could I have this level of skill?" Xu Youyu shook her head repeatedly. "Don't we usually eat at school? On weekends, I either go home for a free meal or find a small restaurant downstairs to sort it out."

"Is your home close to the school, Senior Sister?" Ying Chanxi blinked and asked again.

"It is," Xu Youyu nodded, pointing northwest. "In the faculty housing of Qianjiang University."

"Huh?" Ying Chanxi was taken aback. "Then why rent a place? Isn't Qianjiang University also very close to the First Affiliated High School?"

"Ugh, living at home is so annoying." Xu Youyu waved her hands dismissively. "My parents nag about this and that. It's better to rent and live alone, just for some peace and quiet!"

Li Luo glanced at Xu Youyu, knowing full well what she was thinking.

On one hand, it was because she didn't want to be nagged by her parents, but on the other hand, Li Luo knew very well that Xu Youyu just didn't want her family to find out she was writing webnovels.

Especially since Xu Youyu's father was a renowned professor in the literature department at Qianjiang University, and her mother also came from a scholarly family.

Having been raised in a literary environment, Xu Youyu feared that if her family found out she was writing webnovels in high school, she'd be subjected to family discipline by her parents.

Unlike Li Luo, who with a little persuasion, had made his mom Lin Xiuhong think that writing webnovels was some kind of prestigious novelist endeavor.

Thinking of this, Li Luo couldn't help but smile.

Catching his smile, Xu Youyu couldn't help but ask, "What about you guys? Why did you move here?"

"Because it's closer to the First Affiliated High School," Ying Chanxi said. "But a certain someone probably did it for more convenient access to the computer."

As she spoke, Ying Chanxi turned her head to look at Li Luo, smiling slightly as a reminder, "I'll reset the computer password later. I'll have to supervise you every day to make sure you go to bed on time, otherwise I won't be able to answer to Uncle and Auntie."

"Do you have to be so strict?" Li Luo looked exasperated. "My self-control is very good."

"Since your self-control is so good, my password won't make a difference, right? So what's the harm in setting one?" Ying Chanxi tilted her head and smiled. "Or should I give Auntie a call and ask?"

"That won't be necessary at all." Li Luo waved his hand magnanimously. "Set whatever password you want. It's not like I play much anyway."

Xu Youyu took in the entire scene, chuckling to herself. *You call that playing on the computer?*

*I bet you're secretly typing away every day, aren't you?*
